design.text: Multicenter, open-label, randomized (1:1), active-controlled trial of olaratumab plus doxorubicin versus single-agent doxorubicin.

citations.quote: The primary trial supporting approval, Trial JGDG, is a multicenter, open-label, randomized (1:1), active-controlled trial comparing olaratumab plus doxorubicin to single-agent doxorubicin chemotherapy in patients with advanced STS who have not previously received an anthracycline.

population.text: Adult patients with advanced soft tissue sarcoma (STS) who had not previously received an anthracycline.

citations.quote: a multicenter, open-label trial that randomized (1:1) patients with advanced STS who had not previously received an anthracycline to receive doxorubicin with or without olaratumab.

endpoint.text: Primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS) as assessed by the investigator per RECIST v1.1; overall survival (OS) was a secondary endpoint.

citations.quote: The primary endpoint of Trial JGDG was PFS as assessed by the investigator according to Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version (v) 1.1.
Overall survival (OS), a secondary endpoint, was to be tested at a two-sided alpha level of 5%.

n.text: 133 patients (66 olaratumab plus doxorubicin, 67 single-agent doxorubicin)

citations.quote: The median PFS as assessed by the investigator was improved from 4.1 months (95% CI: 2.8, 5.4) in the single-agent doxorubicin arm (n=67 patients) to 6.6 months (95% CI: 4.1, 8.3) in the olaratumab plus doxorubicin arm (n=66 patients)

result.text: Median PFS 6.6 vs 4.1 months (stratified HR 0.67; 95% CI 0.44, 1.02; two-sided p=0.06); median OS 26.5 vs 14.7 months (unstratified HR 0.52; 95% CI 0.34, 0.79; p<0.05); confirmed ORR by BICR 18.2% vs 7.5%.

citations.quote: The median PFS as assessed by the investigator was improved from 4.1 months (95% CI: 2.8, 5.4) in the single-agent doxorubicin arm (n=67 patients) to 6.6 months (95% CI: 4.1, 8.3) in the olaratumab plus doxorubicin arm (n=66 patients) with a stratified HR of 0.67 (95% CI: 0.44, 1.02; two-sided p-value of 0.06).
with a median OS of 26.5 months (95% CI: 20.9, 31.7) vs. 14.7 months (95% CI: 9.2, 17.1), respectively, and an unstratified HR of 0.52 (95% CI: 0.34, 0.79; p-value <0.05).

Confirmed objective response rates as assessed by BICR were low in both arms: 18.2% (95% CI: 9.8, 29.6) in the olaratumab plus doxorubicin arm and 7.5% (95% CI: 2.5, 16.6) in the single-agent doxorubicin arm.

indication.text: In combination with doxorubicin, for the treatment of adult patients with soft tissue sarcoma (STS) with a histologic subtype for which an anthracycline-containing regimen is appropriate and which is not amenable to curative treatment with radiotherapy or surgery.

citations.quote: LARTRUVO™ is indicated, in combination with doxorubicin, for the treatment of adult patients with soft tissue sarcoma (STS) with a histologic subtype for which an anthracycline-containing regimen is appropriate and which is not amenable to curative treatment with radiotherapy or surgery.

target_moa.text: Olaratumab is a human IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds platelet-derived growth factor receptor alpha (PDGFR-alpha), a receptor tyrosine kinase expressed on cells of mesenchymal origin whose signaling plays a role in cell growth, chemotaxis, and differentiation.

citations.quote: Olaratumab is a human IgG1 antibody that binds platelet-derived growth factor receptor alpha (PDGFR-\alpha). PDGFR-\alpha is a receptor tyrosine kinase expressed on cells of mesenchymal origin. Signaling through this receptor plays a role in cell growth, chemotaxis, and mesenchymal stem cell differentiation.
Olaratumab is a recombinant human IgG1 monoclonal blocking antibody that binds specifically to human platelet-derived growth factor receptor alpha (PDGFR-\alpha).

key_safety.text: Major safety concern is serious infusion-related reactions (IRR: 12.6% any grade, 3.1% Grade 3-4 in the combination arm). Most common adverse reactions (>=20%) were nausea, fatigue, musculoskeletal pain, mucositis, alopecia, vomiting, diarrhea, decreased appetite, abdominal pain, neuropathy, and headache. Grade 3-4 neutropenia was increased with the combination (47% vs 37%).

citations.quote: In Trial JGDG, the incidence of IRR was 12.6% (any grade), including 3.1% Grade 3 or 4 IRR, in the olaratumab plus doxorubicin arm

The most common adverse reactions reported in at least 20% of patients receiving LARTRUVO plus doxorubicin were nausea, fatigue, musculoskeletal pain, mucositis, alopecia, vomiting, diarrhea, decreased appetite, abdominal pain, neuropathy, and headache.
the overall incidence of Grade 3 to 4 neutropenia was increased in the olaratumab plus doxorubicin arm (47%) vs. the single-agent doxorubicin group (37%).

detail.text: A risk evaluation and mitigation strategy (REMS) is not recommended based on the current safety profile of olaratumab.
